cancer_indication: Metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) after ≥2 prior therapies; heavily pretreated hormone receptor–positive/HER2-negative (HR+/HER2−) breast cancer.
drug_class: TROP-2–directed antibody–drug conjugate with SN-38 (topoisomerase I inhibitor) payload
moa: Sacituzumab govitecan (Trodelvy) is an ADC composed of a humanized IgG1 anti–TROP-2 monoclonal antibody linked to SN-38. The antibody binds TROP-2 on tumor cells and triggers rapid internalization; the hydrolysable linker then releases SN-38 intracellularly. SN-38 inhibits DNA topoisomerase I, stabilizing the topoisomerase–DNA cleavage complex and causing DNA single- and double-strand breaks, leading to cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. The Fc portion may also engage Fcγ receptors on immune cells, contributing to antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC).

WP_TROP2_REGULATORY_SIGNALING.description: Trop-2 (TACSTD2) is an epithelial cell-surface antigen that can signal to promote tumor growth via pathways including PKC/MAPK and β-catenin programs and integrin/Src/FAK signaling involved in migration.
WP_TROP2_REGULATORY_SIGNALING.interpretation:
Trop-2 signaling and expression are central to the biology and targeting of many breast cancers (especially TNBC), and Trop-2 surface availability influences ADC binding and internalization in breast cancer.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- Sacituzumab govitecan (SG) is a Trop-2–directed ADC delivering SN-38 to Trop-2–expressing tumor cells. Trop-2 is overexpressed in many epithelial tumors including TNBC and HR⁺/HER2⁻ breast cancer. High/medium Trop-2 expression facilitates antibody binding and internalization and is associated with robust clinical benefit in ASCENT and other trials, although some activity is still seen in lower expressors.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High TACSTD2/Trop-2 signaling/expression in breast tumors increases ADC binding + internalization, improving SN-38 payload delivery and response probability.

MSigDB: WP_TROP2_REGULATORY_SIGNALING (WP5300) (gsea-msigdb.org); DrugBank: DB12893 (Trodelvy MOA/ADC composition) (DrugBank); PMID:33882206 (ASCENT, mTNBC) (PubMed); PMID:37633306 (TROPiCS-02 OS + analyses incl. Trop-2) (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Trop-2 can be high yet functional ADC delivery fails (impaired internalization/lysosomal processing) or cells are payload-resistant (TOP1 alterations, drug-efflux), yielding resistance despite target presence.
PMC: “case study of anti-TROP-2 sacituzumab govitecan” (PMC); Review on TROP-2 ADCs (ScienceDirect)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare (bystander): Even with lower Trop-2, extracellular SN-38 release from cleavable linker can create bystander killing of adjacent cells, producing partial sensitivity.
PMC review/case study (bystander-capable SN-38 ADC concept) (PMC); DrugBank DB12893 (DrugBank)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low Trop-2 reduces binding/internalization → inadequate SN-38 delivery, so tumors behave as primary resistant.
MSigDB WP_TROP2_REGULATORY_SIGNALING (WP5300) (gsea-msigdb.org); DrugBank DB12893 (DrugBank)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Trop-2 engagement triggers internalization and payload release; bulk “Trop-2 signaling” can drop due to receptor trafficking + tumor cell death, consistent with response.
DrugBank DB12893 (DrugBank); PMC anti-TROP-2 SG case study (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Trop-2 pathway scores can fall (e.g., target-positive cells killed), yet residual clones survive via payload resistance/alternative survival circuitry → clinical resistance.
Review on TROP-2 ADCs (ScienceDirect); ASCENT trial paper (clinical resistance exists despite target strategy) PMID:33882206 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible (direct drug action): SG does not activate Trop-2 signaling; any “Up” signal typically reflects more Trop-2+ cells in the sample, not an activating MOA.
DrugBank DB12893 (DrugBank); MSigDB WP5300 context (gsea-msigdb.org)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate (selection/signature-level): Treatment can enrich for Trop-2–high but payload-resistant clones (or non-productive Trop-2 trafficking), yielding an “Up” Trop-2 signature with resistant phenotype.
Review on TROP-2 ADCs (ScienceDirect); PMC anti-TROP-2 SG case study (PMC)

GOMF_DNA_TOPOISOMERASE_ACTIVITY.description: DNA topoisomerase I (TOP1) activity mediates resolution of DNA topological stress by creating transient single-strand breaks and religating DNA; inhibition stabilizes the TOP1–DNA cleavage complex and induces DNA breaks.
GOMF_DNA_TOPOISOMERASE_ACTIVITY.interpretation:
TOP1 activity is directly relevant to the SN-38 payload mechanism in breast cancer, where TOP1 inhibition drives DNA damage, checkpoint activation, and apoptosis.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- SG’s payload SN-38 is a topoisomerase I inhibitor that stabilizes the TOP1–DNA cleavage complex, causing replication-associated DNA breaks and apoptosis in dividing tumor cells. Cells lacking TOP1 or with markedly reduced TOP1 activity are resistant to camptothecins; conversely, abundant functional TOP1 provides more targets for SN-38. Thus, baseline high TOP1 activity is mechanistically compatible with SG sensitivity, though TOP1 expression/activity is not currently used clinically to select breast-cancer patients for SG.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: High DNA topoisomerase activity (often reflecting high TOP1-dependent replication stress) increases vulnerability to SN-38 (TOP1 inhibitor payload).
GO:0003916 “DNA topoisomerase activity” (amigo.geneontology.org); PMC anti-TROP-2 SG case study (SN-38/TOP1 inhibitor payload) (PMC); PMID:33882206 (PubMed)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: Tumors can show high topoisomerase pathway signatures but resist via TOP1 mutations/target remodeling or enhanced DNA-damage tolerance (ATR/CHK1, anti-apoptosis).
GO:0003916 (amigo.geneontology.org); Review on TROP-2 ADCs / payload resistance concepts (ScienceDirect)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: Even if topoisomerase activity is lower, very high intratumoral SN-38 exposure (targeted delivery + bystander) can still induce lethal DNA damage in dividing fractions.
PMC anti-TROP-2 SG case study (PMC); DrugBank DB12893 (DrugBank)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Low proliferation/low TOP1 dependence reduces the effective “target” for SN-38 → primary resistance (common in slow-cycling residual disease states).
GO:0003916 (amigo.geneontology.org); Review on TROP-2 ADCs (ScienceDirect)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: Released SN-38 inhibits TOP1 catalytic function → persistent TOP1-DNA complexes, replication fork collapse, and tumor cell death (response).
PMC anti-TROP-2 SG case study (PMC); DrugBank DB12893 (DrugBank)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: TOP1 activity can be pharmacologically suppressed yet tumors persist due to downstream resistance (apoptosis blockade, repair tolerance, quiescence) → resistant outcome.
Review on TROP-2 ADCs (ScienceDirect); GO:0003916 (amigo.geneontology.org)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible (functional): SN-38 cannot increase functional topoisomerase activity; “Up” typically reflects compensatory TOP1 expression/transcription while enzymatic function remains inhibited.
DrugBank DB12893 (DrugBank); GO:0003916 (amigo.geneontology.org)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Compensatory TOP1 upregulation (or selection for cells with altered TOP1 biology) can accompany resistance, especially if payload effect is blunted by efflux/DNA-damage tolerance.
Review on TROP-2 ADCs (ScienceDirect); ASCENT (resistance patterns exist clinically) PMID:33882206 (PubMed)

REACTOME_GLUCURONIDATION.description: Glucuronidation is a detoxification/metabolic process in which UDP-glucuronosyltransferases (including UGT1A1) conjugate substrates (including SN-38) to glucuronic acid, typically reducing activity and enhancing clearance.
REACTOME_GLUCURONIDATION.interpretation:
Glucuronidation is clinically relevant to SN-38 exposure in breast cancer treatment with sacituzumab govitecan because UGT1A1-mediated inactivation modulates active payload levels and is tied to safety and response-modifying metabolism.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- SN-38 is predominantly inactivated in the liver by UGT1A1 glucuronidation to SN-38G. Increased UGT1A1 activity (e.g., enzyme inducers) accelerates SN-38 clearance and reduces exposure, which is expected to decrease effective systemic anticancer activity of SG; the SG label warns against concomitant strong UGT1A1 inducers for this reason. In contrast, reduced UGT1A1 activity (e.g., UGT1A1*28/*28) increases SN-38 exposure, leading mainly to higher risk of neutropenia and diarrhea. Therefore UGT1A1 is best considered a germline PK/safety factor, not a tumor-cell pathway measurable in the breast tumor transcriptome; its relationship with efficacy for SG in breast cancer remains exploratory.

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare (host dose-intensity): Higher functional UGT1A1/glucuronidation capacity can reduce severe SN-38 toxicity → fewer dose holds, potentially improving delivered dose intensity and outcomes.
Reactome R-HSA-156588 (Reactome); FDA label (UGT1A1-related exposure/toxicity guidance) (FDA Access Data)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: High glucuronidation (UGT-driven SN-38 inactivation to SN-38G) can lower active payload exposure (tumor/host), reducing efficacy → resistance.
Reactome R-HSA-156588 (Reactome); MSigDB: REACTOME_GLUCURONIDATION (gsea-msigdb.org); FDA label (UGT1A1 effects on SN-38 exposure) (FDA Access Data)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate (exposure): Lower glucuronidation can increase active SN-38 exposure, improving tumor kill (with higher toxicity risk).
FDA label (UGT1A1 impacts SN-38 exposure/toxicity; avoid interacting drugs) (FDA Access Data); Reactome R-HSA-156588 (Reactome)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate (clinically limiting toxicity): Low UGT1A1 function can drive severe neutropenia/diarrhea leading to dose reductions/interruptions → reduced effective exposure and poorer efficacy (apparent resistance).
FDA label (UGT1A1-related toxicity/interaction warnings) (FDA Access Data); CPIC/PharmGKB label annotation summary (ClinPGx)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare (tolerability): Glucuronidation increases after dosing because SN-38 is a substrate; adequate host UGT function can limit toxicity while still allowing targeted intratumoral delivery to work.
Reactome R-HSA-156588 (Reactome); Gilead/FDA labeling re: SN-38 metabolism via UGT1A1 (FDA Access Data)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: Increased glucuronidation (or UGT1A1 induction / high UGT activity) lowers active SN-38 exposure → reduced cytotoxic effect and resistance; label warns exposure can drop with UGT1A1 inducers.
FDA label (UGT1A1 inducers reduce SN-38 exposure; avoid) (FDA Access Data); Reactome R-HSA-156588 (Reactome)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare (interaction-driven): Lowering glucuronidation (e.g., via UGT1A1 inhibition) can raise SN-38 exposure and potentially increase tumor kill, but often at the cost of unacceptable toxicity.
FDA label (avoid UGT1A1 inhibitors; toxicity risk) (FDA Access Data); Reactome R-HSA-156588 (Reactome)
Resistance: Mechanistically not possible (as a direct MOA): SG does not directly suppress the host glucuronidation pathway; persistent “Down” typically reflects baseline genetics/liver function rather than drug-driven regulation.
FDA label (UGT1A1 is metabolic pathway; interaction guidance) (FDA Access Data); Reactome R-HSA-156588 (Reactome)

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: High cell-surface Trop-2 increases ADC binding and internalization, increasing intracellular delivery of SN-38.
SN-38 targets the TOP1–DNA complex; active TOP1 is required for DNA cleavage complex stabilization and downstream DNA damage that mediates cytotoxicity.

sensitivity_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Lower UGT1A1 activity reduces SN-38 glucuronidation/inactivation, increasing SN-38 exposure (with increased toxicity risk noted for low-activity UGT1A1*28 homozygosity).
Reduced efflux transporter activity would be expected to retain SN-38 intracellularly, increasing effective exposure to the payload.
Reduced efflux transporter activity would be expected to retain SN-38 intracellularly, increasing effective exposure to the payload.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Upregulated UGT1A1 activity glucuronidates (inactivates) SN-38, lowering active drug levels and thereby contributing to resistance.
Overexpression of drug efflux pumps can increase removal of SN-38, reducing intracellular payload levels and contributing to resistance.
Overexpression of drug efflux pumps can increase removal of SN-38, reducing intracellular payload levels and contributing to resistance.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Downregulation or loss of Trop-2 reduces ADC binding/uptake and can make sacituzumab govitecan ineffective.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR+/HER2− (Luminal A/B): HR+/HER2− (Luminal A/B): These tumors often upregulate hormone-response and proliferation signatures. For example, Luminal A subtypes characteristically show enrichment of focal adhesion pathways (cell–matrix interactions). Luminal B tumors tend to have higher cell-cycle/E2F target activity.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2+: HER2+: These cancers frequently have upregulated ERBB2/HER2 signaling, PI3K/AKT, and MAPK pathway activity, driving rapid growth. Immune signatures are variable.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Triple-negative (Basal-like/TNBC): Triple-negative (Basal-like/TNBC): High expression of inflammatory and proliferative pathways is typical. MSigDB data note that basal/TNBC tumors have upregulated WNT signaling. Other upregulated features in TNBC include TNF-α/NFκB, IL6/JAK/STAT3, and IFNγ-response pathways, along with strong cell-cycle (E2F, G2M) signatures.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.gBRCA1/2-mutated and HRD+ tumors: gBRCA1/2-mutated and HRD+ tumors: These often overlap with TNBC and show high replication stress. Homologous recombination pathways (if intact) may be active, but by definition HRD tumors lack effective HR repair. They frequently upregulate alternative DNA damage responses and cell-cycle checkpoint pathways (e.g. ATR/CHK1) to cope with genomic instability.
